passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypertensol, in adults with stage 1 hypertension. Eighty participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: placebo (n=20), low-dose Hypertensol (25 mg daily, n=20), medium-dose Hypertensol (50 mg daily, n=20), or high-dose Hypertensol (100 mg daily, n=20). Baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) was measured after a 5‑minute seated rest using an automated cuff. After 12 weeks of treatment, SBP was reassessed under identical conditions. Table 1 summarizes the mean SBP values and standard deviations for each group. The placebo group showed a modest mean reduction of 3 mm Hg (SD = 4). In contrast, the low‑dose group experienced a 9 mm Hg reduction (SD = 5), the medium‑dose group a 15 mm Hg reduction (SD = 6), and the high‑dose group a 22 mm Hg reduction (SD = 7). The authors concluded that Hypertensol dose‑dependently lowers SBP, with the high‑dose regimen producing the greatest effect.
table_data:
Group | Mean SBP at Baseline (mmHg) | Mean SBP after 12 weeks (mmHg) | SD (mmHg)
Placebo | 150 | 147 | 4
Low‑dose | 150 | 141 | 5
Medium‑dose | 150 | 135 | 6
High‑dose | 150 | 128 | 7
stem: Based on the data presented, what was the mean systolic blood pressure in the high‑dose Hypertensol group after 12 weeks of treatment?
explanation: The table shows the high‑dose group’s mean SBP after 12 weeks as 128 mm Hg. This is the lowest value among the groups, reflecting the greatest reduction.
trap: Choosing 135 or 147 mmHg by reading the medium-dose or placebo row instead of the high-dose row.

stem: What type of study design was employed in this research?

trap: Calling it a prospective cohort because participants were followed for 12 weeks; investigator-assigned random allocation makes it a trial.

stem: What is the placebo-corrected mean SBP reduction for the medium-dose group?
explanation: Correct: A) Medium-dose reduction = 150 - 135 = 15 mmHg; placebo reduction = 150 - 147 = 3 mmHg; corrected effect = 12 mmHg. Why the others are wrong: B) 15 mmHg ignores the placebo reduction. C) 18 mmHg adds the placebo reduction instead of subtracting it. D) 6 mmHg is the difference between the medium- and low-dose reductions (15 - 9).
trap: Reporting the raw 15 mmHg drop without subtracting the 3 mmHg fall seen with placebo.
